description: Plan an ad: turns a brand and a product or brief into an ad concept, with copy variants (headline, primary text, call to action) and either an image prompt or a timed video storyboard, plus the recipe and the model ids to render with. It renders nothing; pass its output to render_ad, generate_image or generate_video. For a single image ad it is optional: generate_image alone makes one from the saved brand, so skip this step unless the user wants concepts or copy options first. A named length ("a 30 second ad") goes in durationSeconds and the storyboard is written to it; a video with none is not planned: a free question comes back to ask the user (15s is one clip, or 30s, or any 4-180). The user’s own screenshots or pictures to show inside the video go in `inserts`. The brand’s SAVED product photo (get_brand / list_product_photos) is used automatically; never ask the user to upload it again. Uses credits for the planning step.

brand.description: brand name, or a brand profile object {name,domain,category,palette,products,…}. OMIT to use the workspace’s SAVED brand + memory automatically (see get_brand); use draft_brand to onboard a new one

concepts.description: several variants: one line per concept (a different angle each); built exactly

draft.description: Only after a video refusal that offered a lighter draft: the {model, durationSeconds} that refusal named. The plan is then written to that length and priced on that model. Use only the values the refusal gave; when an account cannot cover a video, the refusal comes before planning with three options (an image, adding credits, or this draft when one fits) and the user chooses.

durationSeconds.description: clip length in seconds from that same refusal; use only the value it gave

model.description: video model id from a refusal that offered a lighter draft; use only the value it gave

durationSeconds.description: For video: the total length the user asked for, in whole seconds. The storyboard’s scenes add up to it and the script is sized for it. 4 to 180 seconds; a value outside that is clamped and the reply says so. A length that fits one take of the render model is filmed as one take; a longer one is filmed as the fewest clips that model can take, each a length it can film, joined in order and never sped up.

expected_credits.description: the get_cost price; refused unbilled if the live price differs

get_cost.description: true: return the price only; nothing runs or bills

hook.description: force the VISUAL scroll-stop mechanic the opening beat is built on — a hook id from list_hooks (e.g. "direct_callout", "mid_problem", "macro_asmr"). Omit to let the planner pick. A hook that cannot be delivered in this brief is DROPPED with the reason rather than rendered wrongly — an on-screen-text hook on an authentic/UGC ad is the one that bites, because that register carries zero on-screen text.

idempotency_key.description: chosen once, resent unchanged on retries: the same key never buys twice

inserts.description: VIDEO ONLY: the user's own SCREENS cut in at these seconds (each item's look, kind, start and end say how), the voice running underneath. How many: at most 8, about one per 2.5 s of film (6 s: 2, 10 s: 4, 15 s: 6, 20 s: 8, 30 s: 8), 1.2-2 s each, on the line that talks about it. When there are more, the most crowded are left out first, never the last (the payoff) or one marked key, and the reply names them. The plan keeps those shots free of screens and returns the pictures as creative.inserts for render_ad to lay in (about 2 credits). One that does not fit is left out and the reply says so.

end.description: second it ends: at most 2 s after start (2.5 s full-screen), never in the last 1.5 s of the film

focus.description: the readable part to fill the frame with, as fractions of the picture from its top-left (e.g. the flagged-items table); a crop as tall as wide, or taller, reads best on a phone. Omit for the whole picture, plain margins trimmed

image.description: an https or upload_file URL, a Library id (L0, L1…) or a local path on the CLI

key.description: true = the story needs this one (the payoff): never left out when there are more screens than the length takes

kind.description: screen (default): an app, page, dashboard, document, review or chart. photo: a person, product or place, NOT laid over the video (a product photo goes in as the brand's product photo, a person as a saved creator)

look.description: cutaway (default): a hard cut to the screen filling the frame, cropped to focus, held still, never enlarged past 1.25x its pixels (any gap is the screenshot's own background colour; a screen too small to read is left out and said). card: picture-in-picture over the playing footage, clear of the speaker's face. full: the whole picture uncropped on a blurred backdrop. card and full ONLY when the user asked

start.description: second it appears, never before 1 s (the film opens on moving footage)

language.description: output language for the ad copy (e.g. Spanish) — default English

lengthAsked.description: the user declined to pick a length: use the default

product.description: what to advertise + any angle/offer the user specified

recipe.description: a recipe id from hermoso_capabilities to force an archetype

reference.description: a reference to clone: an ad-library link (Facebook Ad Library, LinkedIn Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency — its real copy/advertiser are fetched) OR a VIDEO link — a TikTok, Instagram Reel, Facebook video, X post or a direct video file (not YouTube: YouTube does not let us download videos, so a YouTube link is refused up front and nothing is charged; the user downloads it themselves and uploads the file (upload_file).) — which is WATCHED first (frames + voiceover/on-screen-text transcript) so the concept keeps its hook, structure and pacing. To remake one video for this brand at its own length, clone_video is the direct tool

setting.description: force the WHERE — a setting id from list_hooks (e.g. "kitchen", "gym", or a surreal one like "volcano_rim" / "airplane_wing", which are played 100% straight and never acknowledged). Omit for a neutral setting.

talent.description: who is on camera; omit to follow the format. Say 'someone new' in product to skip reusing a saved creator.

name: plan_ad
title: Plan an ad concept
